Theorem
[Conservation laws and Riemann invariants] ↗ def:riemann-invariant 1. ch11:11.3-thm-1\group Conservation Laws

The functions $v^1, v^2$ solve the system \[ (6) \qquad \begin{cases} v^1_t + \lambda _2(\mathbf{u})v^1_x = 0 \\ v^2_t + \lambda _1(\mathbf{u})v^2_x = 0 \end{cases} \quad \text{in } \mathbb {R}\times (0,\infty ). \] Thus the system is diagonal in the Riemann coordinates.

Proof

\sketch For $i\ne j$, the chain rule and (1) give

\[ v^i_t+\lambda _j(\mathbf u)v^i_x =Dw^i(\mathbf u)\bigl(-D\mathbf F(\mathbf u)+\lambda _j(\mathbf u)I\bigr)\mathbf u_x. \]

By definition $Dw^i$ is parallel to the left eigenvector $l_j$, so the last expression vanishes.

□
